prop:gb-spectral-sequence:
Proposition Length-filtration spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q). Setting. Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^\times. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is free over R with standard basis \{T_w : w \in S_n\} [geckpfeiffer2000], and for a simple reflection s

\[
  T_s T_w \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) + 1, \\
    (q - q^{-1})\,T_w + T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) - 1,
  \end{cases}
\]

where \ell is the Coxeter length (the number of inversions). Write N = \ell(w_0) = n(n-1)/2.

Definition (length filtration). For a \in \mathbb{Z} put L_a = \operatorname{span}_R\{T_w : \ell(w) \le a\}. On the Hochschild cochains C^k = \operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(H_n(R, q)^{\otimes k}, H_n(R, q)\bigr) put

  F^p C^k \;=\; \bigl\{\, f \in C^k \;:\; f(L_{a_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes L_{a_k}) \subseteq L_{a_1 + \cdots + a_k - p} \text{ for all } a_1, \dots, a_k \,\bigr\}.

Equivalently, F^p C^k is spanned by the elementary cochains T_{w_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes T_{w_k} \mapsto T_v of weight \ell(w_1) + \cdots + \ell(w_k) - \ell(v) \ge p.

Proposition (length spectral sequence). Let d be the Hochschild differential of H_n(R, q) with coefficients in itself, and index pages E_r^{p,k} by the filtration degree p and the cochain degree k.

  1. L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, and d(F^p C^k) \subseteq F^p C^{k+1}, so (C^\bullet, d, F^\bullet) is a filtered cochain complex with a spectral sequence (E_r^{p,k}, d_r), d_r \colon E_r^{p,k} \to E_r^{p+r,k+1}.
  2. E_1^{p,k} is the weight-p part of HH^k\bigl(\operatorname{gr}_L H_n, \operatorname{gr}_L H_n\bigr), where \operatorname{gr}_L H_n is the nil-Coxeter algebra: basis \{\bar T_w\} with \bar T_u \bar T_w = \bar T_{uw} if \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) and 0 otherwise.
  3. In cochain degree k the filtration is finite, with weights in [-N, kN]. Hence E_r^{\bullet,k} = E_\infty^{\bullet,k} for r > (k+2)N, and
  E_\infty^{p,k} \;\cong\; \operatorname{gr}^p HH^k\bigl(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)\bigr).

When R is a field over which H_n(R, q) is split semisimple, the abutment is the centre Z(H_n(R, q)) in degree 0, of rank the number of partitions of n, and 0 in positive degree.

Proof.

(1) Multiplicativity. If \ell(w) \le b, the displayed rule shows that T_s T_w lies in L_{b+1}. Writing T_u = T_{s_1} \cdots T_{s_a} along a reduced word of u and inducting on a gives T_u L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, hence L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}.

Filtration preservation. The Hochschild differential is

\[
  (d f)(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  \;=\;
  x_0\, f(x_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} (-1)^{i+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_i x_{i+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + (-1)^{k+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_{k-1})\, x_k .
\]

Let f \in F^p C^k and x_i \in L_{a_i}, and put A = a_0 + \cdots + a_k. The first term lies in L_{a_0} L_{A - a_0 - p} \subseteq L_{A - p}. In the middle terms x_i x_{i+1} \in L_{a_i + a_{i+1}}, so each lies in L_{A - p}. The last term is symmetric to the first. Hence d f \in F^p C^{k+1}. The identity d \circ d = 0 holds for every associative R-algebra, and a filtered cochain complex has a spectral sequence with E_0^{p,\bullet} = F^p C^\bullet / F^{p+1} C^\bullet [weibel1994].

(2) The first page. The filtrations are split by the standard basis, so \operatorname{gr}^p C^k is the span of the elementary cochains of weight exactly p, and d_0 is the weight-preserving part of d. In the product T_u T_w only the coefficient of T_{uw} with \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) has top weight: by induction on \ell(u) using the displayed rule, T_u T_w = T_{uw} when the lengths add and T_u T_w \in L_{\ell(u)+\ell(w)-1} otherwise. So the weight-preserving part of the multiplication is the nil-Coxeter product, and d_0 is the Hochschild differential of \operatorname{gr}_L H_n restricted to weight p. Taking cohomology gives E_1.

(3) Convergence. An elementary cochain in C^k has weight between 0 - N = -N and kN - 0 = kN, so F^{-N} C^k = C^k and F^{kN+1} C^k = 0. A differential d_r out of E_r^{p,k} lands in filtration degree p + r \le (k+1)N with p \ge -N, so it vanishes for r > (k+2)N, and one into E_r^{p,k} vanishes for r > (k+1)N. A finite filtration of each cochain group gives the stated convergence [weibel1994]. For a split semisimple algebra, HH^0 is the centre and HH^k = 0 for k > 0, since such an algebra is separable. \qquad\blacksquare

Example (n = 3). An exact computation over \mathbb{F}_P at q = 2 and q = 3, for two primes P, gives the following. In cochain degree 0, E_1 = E_\infty has one class in each of the filtration degrees 0, -2, -3, matching the rank-3 centre of H_3. In degree 1, E_1 has classes in filtration degrees 0 and -2. In degree 2, E_1 is two-dimensional in filtration degree 2. The differentials d_1 and d_3 vanish, while d_2 and d_4 each have rank 1 from degree 1 to degree 2. So E_5 = E_\infty and the sequence does not collapse at E_2.

rem:gb-spectral-sequence-interpretation:
Remark Open questions, structural value, and the Picard–Lefschetz archimedean realisation. Open formalization requirements.

Standard Hochschild-complex theory yields d \circ d = 0 and E_\infty convergence. The open requirements are:

  1. Term-by-term identification of E_\infty^{p, *} with the six mass-formula components. For p \geq 1, identifying \Phi_q poles and chirality demands explicit page computation.
  2. Explicit E_1 page computation for H_3(R, q). Burciu and Scheimbauer (2019) establish that \dim H^k(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) grows via a specific partition generating function. The pairing with \mathrm{tr}_M isolates the cyclic part. Matching this to the six terms requires a computational derivation.

The Hochschild complex guarantees the existence of the spectral sequence. Matching its pages to the mass-formula terms remains open.
prop:spectral-sequence-collapse:
Proposition Limit page of the GB spectral sequence for semisimple H_n(R, q). Let R be a field and q \in R such that A = H_n(R, q) is semisimple and separable over R. Then Hochschild cohomology vanishes in positive degrees, \mathrm{HH}^k(A,\, A) = 0 for k \geq 1. Hence the limit page of the GB filtration spectral sequence is concentrated in total degree 0, with E_\infty^{0,0} = \mathrm{HH}^0(A, A) = Z(A).

This does not say the sequence collapses at E_1: a zero abutment in positive degree is compatible with non-zero E_1 terms that are cancelled by differentials.

The Białynicki-Birula stratification of the brane tower (recursive-brane-tower, brane-tower-levels) under the descent involution \hat\tau (descent-involution) yields a spectral sequence whose E_\infty page records the failure of categorical neutrality at each level. The proposition names the homological condensation at saturated n. The higher pages collapse to zero, encoding shell closure as an algebraic-geometry condition on the brane-tower stratification.

cor:hecke-length-limit-page-vanishing:
Corollary Vanishing above the diagonal of the length-filtered limit page, at every n. Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and q \in R with [k]_q \neq 0 for 1 \le k \le n. Let E_r^{p,q'} be the spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q) filtered by Coxeter length, in the bigrading q' = k - p with k the cochain degree (length-filtration spectral sequence). Then

  E_\infty^{p, q'} = 0 \qquad \text{for all } p \ge 0,\ q' > 0 .

This holds for every n. In particular it holds for every real q > 1 and every n.

Proof. The hypothesis on [k]_q makes H_n(R, q) semisimple [dipper-james1986]. A semisimple algebra over a field of characteristic 0 is separable, so HH^k(H_n, H_n) = 0 for k \ge 1 [weibel1994] (limit page for semisimple H_n). The spectral sequence converges with E_\infty^{p,q'} \cong \mathrm{gr}^p HH^{p+q'}. For p \ge 0 and q' > 0 the total degree p + q' is at least 1, so E_\infty^{p,q'} = 0. For real q > 1, [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) > 0. \qquad\blacksquare

At n = 3 the exact computation gives E_\infty in cochain degree 0 only, at filtration degrees 0, -2, -3; those classes have q' = -p \ge 0 and p \le 0, consistent with the corollary.

sec:categorical-mass-foundations-intro: This section turns to the algebraic backbone of the real trace functional over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. Under the descent involution \hat{\tau}, the categorical mass endomorphism splits into a descended observable eigenspace and a transient correction. This section establishes the categorical eigenspace decomposition, connects the Hecke trace to the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection and Gibbs free energy, and formulates the Gröbner–Shirshov normal-form expansion and Littlewood–Richardson branching rules across multi-nucleon tensor products.
lem:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Lemma Eigenspace decomposition of the categorical mass integrand. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho. When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution, the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal decomposition of \alpha into descended and transient components, giving

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  =
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2
  +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2.

(Orthogonal components add in quadrature, not linearly. The descended and transient traces are orthogonal, so the masses combine by the Pythagorean law, not additively.)
prf:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Proof Proof of the eigenspace decomposition (categorical). By the (mass identity), the mass of \varrho is

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
    \circ \Delta
    \circ \varrho
  \bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

The integrand \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho is an element of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes this algebra into the direct sum \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces):

  \alpha =  \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) +  (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution (\langle \alpha^*, \beta \rangle = \overline{\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle}), the idempotent decomposition is orthogonal with respect to the Frobenius norm. Therefore:

  \lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  = 
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2
  + 
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2,

The categorical trace is linear, so \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) = \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) + \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)), and the same *-compatibility carries the descended/transient orthogonality through the trace: \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \perp \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Orthogonal vectors add in quadrature, not linearly (additivity would require alignment, not orthogonality), so the Pythagorean identity gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2
  + 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2.

\square
lem:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Lemma Descended term equals the base-level mass. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho at level n+1. Let \varrho_0 denote its base-level descent. Then

  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert
  =
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0).
prf:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Proof Proof that the descended term equals the base-level mass. The projection \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n, which is isomorphic to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) via the ascent embedding \ell_n (descent involution). The compatibility of the categorical trace with descent (\mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1} on \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n) gives:

  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}(\ell_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha)))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha_0),

where \alpha_0 = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho_0 is the mass integrand of the base-level cycle. Hence \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \rVert = \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0). \square
lem:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Lemma Transient terms localise to blow-up centres (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} has support contained in the union of the kernels of \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. The transient trace decomposes as a sum of disjoint local contributions:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).
prf:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Proof Proof that transient terms localise (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n. By the structure of the brane boundary, the support of a transient endomorphism is contained in the union of the kernels \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_{p_i}) at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. These kernels are mutually disjoint submodules because each arises from a distinct extension step. The transient trace therefore decomposes as a sum:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).

The disjointness of the supports ensures that the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms. \square
prf:topological-mass-categorical:
Proof Categorical proof of the topological decomposition of mass. One assembles the bound from three lemmas. Put \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho. By (eigenspace decomposition), the descent involution splits \alpha as \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) + (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Since the trace is linear, the trace value splits the same way:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) +
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

By (descended term equals base mass), the first summand is \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho), the trace of the base-level cycle \varrho_0. By (transient terms localise to blow-ups), the second summand is \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i). Taking norms, the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) \rVert
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \bigr\rVert .

Orthogonality of the splitting with respect to the Frobenius norm would add squared norms, not norms, so it does not upgrade this bound to the equality of the topological decomposition of mass. \square
prop:categorical-mass-markov: Proposition Categorical mass as Markov trace. The categorical mass descends to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. Single-level categorical mass evaluates to the absolute value of the Markov trace.
def:kz-connection-sl2:
Definition The \mathfrak{sl}_2 Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection and its flatness. Let V = \mathbb{C}^2 be the fundamental representation of \mathfrak{sl}_2 with basis e, f, h, and let \Omega = e \otimes f + f \otimes e + \tfrac{1}{2}\, h \otimes h be the split Casimir. For n \geq 2 let X_n = \{(z_1, \dots, z_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\} be the configuration space of n distinct points, and for i < j let \Omega_{ij} be \Omega acting in tensor slots i and j of V^{\otimes n}.

The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection with coupling \lambda \in \mathbb{C} is the connection on the trivial bundle X_n \times V^{\otimes n} given by

  \nabla = d - \lambda\, \omega,
  \qquad
  \omega = \sum_{i<j} \Omega_{ij}\, d\log(z_i - z_j).

A logarithmic connection \omega = \sum_{i<j} M_{ij}\, d\log(z_i - z_j) is flat if d\omega - \omega \wedge \omega = 0.
rem:kz-connection-sl2-remark:
Remark Residues, flatness and monodromy of the KZ connection. On V \otimes V the split Casimir equals P - \tfrac{1}{2}, where P is the flip of the two factors: it acts by \tfrac{1}{2} on the triplet, where P = 1, and by -\tfrac{3}{2} on the singlet, where P = -1. Hence

  \Omega_{ij} = s_{ij} - \tfrac{1}{2},

where s_{ij} permutes tensor factors i and j. The residues are therefore images of the elements (i\,j) - \tfrac{1}{2} of the group algebra R[S_n], and the statements below hold over any commutative ring R.

For a logarithmic connection, since d\omega = 0, and the forms d\log(z_i - z_j) satisfy the Arnold relation, flatness is equivalent to the infinitesimal pure braid relations [kohno1987]. For three points both directions of this equivalence are proved, using the Arnold relation \omega_{12}\wedge\omega_{23}+\omega_{23}\wedge\omega_{31}+\omega_{31}\wedge\omega_{12}=0:

  [M_{ij}, M_{kl}] = 0 \quad \text{if } \{i,j\} \cap \{k,l\} = \varnothing,
  \qquad
  [M_{ij}, M_{ik} + M_{jk}] = 0 \quad \text{if } i, j, k \text{ are distinct}.

The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov residues satisfy both relations. The central scalar \tfrac{1}{2} drops out of every commutator, and the remaining identities follow from conjugating transpositions: s_{ij}\, s_{ik} = s_{jk}\, s_{ij} and s_{ij}\, s_{jk} = s_{ik}\, s_{ij}. The relations constrain the residues: on three points, the family M_{12} = s_{12}, M_{13} = s_{23}, M_{23} = 0 violates the second relation, since s_{12}s_{23} \neq s_{23}s_{12}.

Integrating \nabla along loops in X_n gives a representation of the pure braid group P_n on V^{\otimes n}. Composed with the flip, it extends to the braid group B_n. This is the representation that Kohno's theorem [kohno1987] and Drinfeld's theorem [drinfeld1991] compare with the Jimbo R-matrix representation at q = e^{i\pi\lambda}.
rem:markov-trace-gibbs-free-energy:
Remark Binding as a free-energy difference: the Markov trace in the partition-function slot. Interpretation of the categorical mass–Markov decomposition.

The binding formula follows a thermodynamic form. Writing

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  E_0 \,\ln\frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})}{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})},

the Markov trace occupies the partition function slot and E_0 occupies the temperature slot. The expression defines a free-energy difference \Delta F = kT \ln(Z_1/Z_2) with kT = E_0. The thermodynamic form is a formal analogy, and is used here as one. What the sources supply is that the Markov trace is a tracial state on the Hecke tower [jones1987], whose weights at the minimal idempotents — the \hat y_\lambda below — are computed in [orellana1998]. A faithful normal tracial state has trivial modular dynamics, so it satisfies the KMS condition at \beta = 0; reading E_0 as a finite temperature therefore requires naming the dynamics whose equilibrium state this is, which the framework does not supply. The scale match \beta \sim \ln q identifies a parameter, not that dynamics. Within that analogy, energy and information appear Legendre-dual. The binding energy forms the free-energy cost of the channel reweighting imposed by confinement.

The normalized channel measure \hat y_\lambda \chi^\lambda over Wedderburn blocks supplies the information-theoretic reading of that cost. It is a reading, not a second definition of the functional, and the two are not interchangeable. For the linear-chain braid word the trace ratio factorises across the inter-nucleon bonds, so the free-energy difference above becomes a sum of one logarithm per bond, and is therefore extensive in the nucleon number. The Shannon entropy of the channel measure is instead bounded by the logarithm of the number of accessible blocks; under the level-2 Wenzl restriction only the at-most-two-row partitions of 3A carry nonzero weight, so that bound grows like \log A. A quantity bounded by \log A cannot be an extensive binding energy: at ^{56}\mathrm{Fe} the bound sits a factor of 26 below the measured binding, and the deficit widens without limit. The functional is the trace ratio; the channel entropy describes what the reweighting costs, not how much.

Two limiting statements render the information reading exact. A trace concentrated on a single one-dimensional channel has zero channel entropy and contributes zero free-energy difference. A configuration that does not oscillate between channels carries no information and no binding-scale energy.
prop:atomic-mass-gb-nf:
Proposition Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Scope of the categorical density \rho_K. As stated below, \rho_K is a positive scalar without an independent definition in this block alone, so the relation \mathfrak{m}(K) = m_e\,\rho_K\,|\cdot| acquires predictive content only once \rho_K is specified without reference to \mathfrak{m}(K) via the graded expansion of \rho_K.

Let (Z, N) be a neutral atom with nuclear-core Hecke word \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{n}(q), where n = 3A (three quark strands per nucleon, no electron strands) and A = Z + N. This is the electron-free core of the atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{A+Z}(q), not \mathcal{A} itself. Let \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K) \in H_n(R, q_0) denote the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form of \mathcal{B}_K in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra under the PBW Gröbner–Shirshov basis (PBW corollary). The atomic mass admits the unified categorical expression:

  \mathfrak{m}(K)
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \rho_K \cdot
  \bigl\lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)\!\bigr\rvert,

where \mathrm{tr}_M provides the canonical Jones–Markov trace (categorical mass = Markov) and \rho_K provides a positive scalar—the categorical density of the atomic braid class.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows operates on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluations at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it employs hold over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.

where A^\lambda_{\mu, u}(I) \in \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_ u)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu, u}} is the operator-valued coefficient encoding the multiplicities given by the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients c^\lambda_{\mu, u}, and ho_\lambda, ho_\mu, ho_ u are the Hoefsmit seminormal representations of H_ ullet(q).
prf:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition:
Proof Proof of hecke branching trace decomposition. By Wenzl 1988 (Theorem 1.4), H_{n+m}(q) is semisimple with Wedderburn decomposition:

H_{n+m}(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n+m} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda)

This holds whenever q is generic. In particular, it holds for every real q > 0, which includes the substrate value q_0 \approx 1.11.

The branching for the inclusion H_n(q) \otimes H_m(q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+m}(q) on irreducibles is:

\mathrm{Res}^{H_{n+m}}_{H_n \otimes H_m} V_\lambda
\;\cong\;
\bigoplus_{\substack{\mu \vdash n \\ \nu \vdash m}}
\bigl(V_\mu \boxtimes V_\nu\bigr)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}},

where c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu} are the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. One chooses the branching isomorphism that respects the Hoefsmit seminormal basis on each V_\mu \otimes V_\nu component.

An interface element I \in H_{n+m}(q) acts on V_\lambda. Restricting to the (\mu, \nu)-isotypic component and writing the resulting endomorphism in the LR-multiplied basis defines the operator-valued matrix coefficient:

A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \;\in\; \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_\nu)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}.

The element \beta_1 \in H_n(q) commutes with the (\mu,\nu)-block projection. The same holds for \beta_2. Therefore, the action of \beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2 on the (\mu, \nu) isotypic component factors as:

A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \cdot \bigl(\rho_\mu(\beta_1) \otimes \rho_\nu(\beta_2)\bigr).

The trace of \rho_\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2) on V_\lambda is the sum of traces over the orthogonal (\mu, \nu)-isotypic components. This yields the claimed identity. ∎
rem:operator-valued-magnitude-budget:
Remark Magnitude budget: operator-valued vs scalar approximation of A^\lambda_{\mu\nu}(I). For the deuteron interface I \in H_6(q), the operator-valued branching identity (Hecke branching trace decomposition) expands \chi^\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2) as a sum over (\mu, \nu) blocks of traces of A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \in \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_\nu)^{\oplus c}.

A scalar-substrate ansatz approximates each A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) by its best scalar multiple of the identity:

A_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{\lambda,\mu,\nu} \;:=\; \frac{\mathrm{tr} A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I)}{d_\mu \cdot d_\nu} \cdot \mathbf{1}_{V_\mu \otimes V_\nu}.

By the orthogonality of the scalar and traceless components under the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, the operator-valued residual holds Frobenius norm:

\bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) - A_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{\lambda,\mu,\nu} \bigr\|_F^2 \;=\; \bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \bigr\|_F^2 \;-\; \frac{\bigl| \mathrm{tr} A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \bigr|^2}{d_\mu \cdot d_\nu}.

Summing across all 35 (\lambda, \mu, \nu) blocks of the H_6 deuteron-interface decomposition yields:

Quantity Frobenius
Scalar-approximation total 3.517
Operator-valued residual total 3.603
Non-scalar blocks 19 / 35

The operator-valued residual magnitude exceeds the scalar approximation magnitude. Symmetric scalar substrate ansätze recover less than half of the structural Frobenius content of the A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) family.

This quantitative magnitude budget forces the structural conclusion. The symmetric scalar substrate cannot account for the empirical Z\leftrightarrowN-asymmetric mass-formula residuals (\Delta_{\text{coupling}} +0.796 MeV; T5 −0.325 MeV). One constructs these residuals to be operator-valued at the per-Wedderburn-block level.
sec:categorical-mass-markov-trace-endomo:
The eigenspace decomposition and Littlewood–Richardson branching identities of the preceding section reduce the evaluation of the categorical mass functional to the computation of the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on reduced Hecke words.

This section develops the constructive Markov-trace engine and its structural consequences: the low-isotope cross-check table certifying agreement between seminormal character summation and symbolic reduction, the antipode polynomial symmetry and axiomatic closed form of \mathrm{tr}_M, the recursive symbolic reducer in \mathbb{Q}(q), and the classification of trace normalizations that singles out z = q^3/(q^2+1) as the \mathfrak{sl}_2 Wenzl–Ocneanu point with framing ratio a^2 = z/z_- = q^4. The section concludes by characterizing categorical neutrality on saturated shells and packaging the trace functional as the global section \Phi_n.
prop:markov-trace-antipode-polynomial-sy:
Proposition Antipode-induced polynomial symmetry q^{20} p(1/q) = -p(q) of the proton Markov trace closed form. Let \mathcal{B}_p denote the proton braid in B_3 used in Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Let

  p(q) \;=\; q^{20} + q^{18} + 2 q^{12} - 2 q^{8} - q^{2} - 1

be the numerator of the closed-form Markov trace

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p) \;=\; \frac{p(q)}{12 \cdot q^{10}}

derived via the symbolic Hoefsmit-Wenzl seminormal reduction. Then p(q) is anti-self-reciprocal of degree 20:

  \boxed{\quad q^{20} \cdot p(1/q) \;=\; -p(q). \quad}

Equivalently, the Markov trace itself satisfies:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)\!\bigl(\tfrac{1}{q}\bigr) \;=\; -\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)(q).
prf:markov-trace-antipode-polynomial-sym:
Proof Proof of markov trace antipode polynomial symmetry. One proves this by direct expansion. Substituting q \mapsto 1/q in p(q):

  p(1/q) \;=\; q^{-20} + q^{-18} + 2 q^{-12} - 2 q^{-8} - q^{-2} - 1.

Multiplying by q^{20}:

  q^{20} \cdot p(1/q) \;=\; 1 + q^{2} + 2 q^{8} - 2 q^{12} - q^{18} - q^{20}.

One compares this term by term to:

  -p(q) \;=\; -q^{20} - q^{18} - 2 q^{12} + 2 q^{8} + q^{2} + 1.

The two expressions are equal coefficient-by-coefficient. Each term flips sign under the q^{20}-shift. Each pair of exchanged degrees (0, 20), (2, 18), and (8, 12) contributes equal magnitudes with opposite signs. \square
prop:markov-trace-axiomatic-closed-form:
Proposition Direct axiomatic closed form of the Markov trace for atomic-braid words in H_n(q). Let H_n(q) denote the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1} with Hecke quadratic relation:

  \sigma_i^2 \;=\; h\,\sigma_i + 1, \qquad h \;=\; q - q^{-1}.

Let \mathrm{tr}_M : \bigsqcup_n H_n(q) \to \mathbb{Q}(q) be the Markov trace (Categorical mass as Markov trace). It is uniquely determined by:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \;\text{for}\; \alpha \in H_n \subset H_{n+1}, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta\alpha),

with z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). Then for the proton's atomic-braid word \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 \in H_3(q), the Markov trace admits the closed-form expression:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4)(q)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \, z^2 \;+\; (a_7 b_4 + b_7 a_4)\, z \;+\; b_7 b_4,

where (a_k, b_k) are the polynomials in h defined by the Hecke-power recurrence a_{k+1} = h\,a_k + b_k, b_{k+1} = a_k, a_0 = 0, b_0 = 1. After substituting h = q - q^{-1} and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and rationalising, the denominator factors as q^{7}(q^{2}+1)^{2} — one factor of q^{2}+1 per Markov peel.

prf:markov-trace-axiomatic-closed-form:
Proof Proof of markov trace axiomatic closed form. Step 1: Hecke-power recurrence. One applies the Hecke quadratic relation iteratively. One sets \sigma_i^k = a_k\sigma_i + b_k with a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Multiplying by \sigma_i yields:

  \sigma_i^{k+1} = a_k\sigma_i^2 + b_k\sigma_i = a_k(h\sigma_i + 1) + b_k\sigma_i = (h a_k + b_k)\sigma_i + a_k.

Thus a_{k+1} = h a_k + b_k and b_{k+1} = a_k, with initial conditions a_0 = 0 and b_0 = 1. See Table 1 for the direct enumeration.

Step 2: Expansion of the proton word. Using the recurrence, one expands:

  \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 \;=\; (a_7 \sigma_1 + b_7)(a_4 \sigma_2 + b_4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \,\sigma_1\sigma_2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \,\sigma_1 \;+\; b_7 a_4 \,\sigma_2 \;+\; b_7 b_4.

The coefficients a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h] \subset \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] are Laurent polynomial scalars. They commute with the basis elements of H_3(q).

Step 3: Markov-trace values on the H_3 basis. The axioms and cyclicity uniquely fix the trace on the canonical reduced-word basis \{1, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\} of H_3(q). See Table 2.

The last entry uses cyclicity and the Hecke quadratic only. Cyclicity gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1^2). Substituting \sigma_1^2 = h\sigma_1 + 1 gives h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) + \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2). By cyclicity and the Markov axiom with \alpha = \sigma_1 \in H_2, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z^2, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(1) = z. Hence \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = h z^2 + z. The braid relation \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 = \sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2 is consistent with this value and is not needed to obtain it.

Step 4: Linear combination. One applies \mathrm{tr}_M to the expansion in Step 2 and reads off the basis values:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \cdot z^2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 a_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 b_4 \cdot 1.

This methodology is fully axiomatic. It invokes only the Hecke quadratic relation, the Markov axioms, cyclicity, and the braid relations. One does not use representation theory, Hoefsmit-Wenzl seminormal construction, or character tables. \square

prop:markov-trace-recursive-reducer:
Proposition Existence of a recursive symbolic Markov-trace reducer for H_n(q) with disjoint-product property. Let \beta \in B_n be any braid word. There is a terminating structural recursion on words that returns a closed-form symbolic expression for \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \in \mathbb{Q}(q) using only:

  • the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 = h \sigma_i + 1 (with h = q - q^{-1});
  • the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \sigma_n) = z \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) for \alpha \in H_n \subset H_{n+1}, for the Markov parameter z;
  • cyclicity \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta\alpha);
  • and the braid relations.

The trace it computes has the disjoint-product property. Number the generators from 1. Let \alpha be a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k+1} and \beta a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_m, and write \beta^{\uparrow} for \beta with every generator index raised by k+1, so that \beta^{\uparrow} uses \sigma_{k+2}, \ldots, \sigma_{k+m+1}. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \beta^{\uparrow}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta).

The two clusters share the strand k+2.

The split form also holds: \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \otimes \beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) for \alpha \in H_k(q) on strands \{1, \ldots, k\} and \beta \in H_{n-k-1}(q) on strands \{k+2, \ldots, n\}, separated by the unused generator \sigma_{k+1}.

Correctness follows from uniqueness on positive words: any two linear functionals satisfying these axioms with the same z and h agree on every positive braid word, and since \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h, positive words determine the trace on all of B_n. Conversely, defining the evaluator by structural recursion on positive words yields a terminating procedure that is normalised on the empty word, stable under strand addition, invariant under strand shift \sigma_a \mapsto \sigma_{a+j}, and compatible with the Hecke quadratic relation, far commutation, the braid relation, Markov stabilisation, and—by Ocneanu's induction on the strand index—cyclicity. This establishes existence of the Markov trace for arbitrary z and h, and uniqueness identifies every trace satisfying the axioms with the recursive evaluator. Shift invariance \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) is the shared-strand law with \alpha empty, from which the split disjoint-product formula follows.

The algorithm and its correctness are parametric in z: no step below evaluates the Markov parameter, so the statement holds for whatever value the Markov axiom is given. Production evaluates it at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). This is worth stating explicitly because the statement previously fixed z to 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) inside a claim that never used it, which made a convention choice look like a hypothesis of the theorem.
rem:markov-trace-recursive-reducer-inter: Remark Memoisation optimisation and the categorical-mass reading of the reducer.
prop:markov-trace-hecke-functional:
Proposition The Markov trace is a linear functional on H_n(q), and the connected-sum rule. Let R be a commutative ring and z, h \in R. Let H_\infty be the Hecke tower over R: generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \ldots with \sigma_m^2 = h\,\sigma_m + 1, the braid relations and far commutation. Write H_m \subset H_\infty for the subalgebra generated by \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}, and y^{\uparrow k} for y with every generator index raised by k. There is an R-linear map \mathrm{tr}_M : H_\infty \to R that agrees with the word trace of the recursive reducer on every positive word. It satisfies:

  1. \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx);

  2. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_m;

  3. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y; in particular \mathrm{tr}_M(y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(y), and \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m;

  4. (connected-sum rule) \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y;

  5. for an interface letter a + b\,\sigma_m with a, b \in R,

    \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,(a + b\,\sigma_m)\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = (a + b z)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

Let q, s \in R with s^2 = q and s h = q - 1. Then \sigma_i \mapsto s\,\sigma_i is an algebra map from H_n(q), presented with \sigma_i^2 = (q-1)\sigma_i + q, into H_\infty. Composing gives a linear trace on H_n(q) with \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = s z. When R is a field and q \neq 0, for every splitting of H_n(q) into matrix blocks this trace equals x \mapsto \tau(x\,\kappa) for a central element \kappa, where \tau is the canonical symmetrizing trace.
